chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality.
He said: “Except if she commits adultery, then she is to be expelled, and the hadd is to be carried out upon her.”

key_terms.اتَّقُوا: Have taqwa; fear and be conscious of Allah in observing His ruling
key_terms.بُيُوتِهِنَّ: Their houses; the residences in which they remain during the waiting period
key_terms.فَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ: A clear immorality; here explained as adultery
key_terms.لَا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ: Do not expel them; a prohibition against turning divorced women out of their houses

ai.seo_question: What does 'a clear immorality' mean in Qur'an 65:1 according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic exception in the ruling that a divorced woman is not to be expelled from her house during her waiting period. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام interprets the 'clear immorality' mentioned in the verse as adultery, in which case expulsion and the legal hadd punishment apply.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4759 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: "And fear Allah (swt), your Lord (azj). Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave unless they commit a clear immorality" (Surah At-Talaq 65:1).
Imam (as) replied: "Except if she commits adultery, then she is to be expelled, and the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is to be carried out upon her."
